messages:
incident-bot: HIGH: multi-gpu job failures detected on cluster-gpu-prod (alert rule: nccl_comm_errors > 5m). Examples: <> NCCL TIMEOUT, CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION, container restart. Auto-page: @sre-oncall :rotating_light:

sre-oncall: on it. seeing multiple pods in CrashLoopBackOff with `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION` and NCCL timeouts. tagging runtime/infra.

raj (runtime): logs from pod runtime-abc-7ffd:
```
I0215 14:02:11.123456 1 communicator.cc:432] NCCL WARN timeout at barrier 0x7f8c122
E0215 14:02:11.123789 1 cuda_driver.cc:88] cudaSetDevice() failed: CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION
E0215 14:02:12.000000 1 runtime_server.cc:214] Unhandled exception: cuda driver lost
```

kubectl get pods -n redwood-serving | grep runtime-abc

kevin (eng-runtime): node traces show GPU reset + driver messages on node gpu-n3-17:
```
$ dmesg | tail -n 20
[ 12345.678901] NVRM: GPU at 0000:65:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 12345.678905] NVRM: GPU 0000:65:00.0: GPU panic - reason 0x2, but reboot suppressed
[ 12345.679000] nvidia 0000:65:00.0: GPU reset (Xid 79)
```

incident-bot: Impact metrics: increase in 5xx for /v1/generate for tp4 models ~15% over baseline; ~3 customers affected (customer-42, customer-88, customer-proto).

aisha (ml-infra): hypothesis: recent kernel/driver rollout to gpu-n3 pool (2026-02-14 23:10 UTC) + NCCL async behavior causing communicator hangs under tp+pp split. could be interplay with NV driver new Xid handling.

maria (support): raised CS tickets for the 3 customers and started template message. They want ETA.

sre-oncall: immediate mitigation plan:
1) Remove affected nodes from scheduler (cordon + drain for non-critical pods).
2) Restart runtime pods with env overrides to force NCCL async error handling and verbose logs: NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1 NCCL_DEBUG=INFO NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=SYS
3) Failover long-running TP shards to single-node fallback model (canary) using routing policy.
4) If driver still unstable, rollback driver to previous package on gpu-n3 pool.

raj (runtime): adding suggested quick commands:
```
kubectl cordon gpu-n3-17
kubectl drain gpu-n3-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data
kubectl rollout restart deploy/runtime-model-tp4 -n redwood-serving
# restart with patched env
kubectl set env deploy/runtime-model-tp4 -n redwood-serving NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1 NCCL_DEBUG=INFO NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=SYS
```

kevin (eng-runtime): note: restarting all pods will spike latency. prefer targeted restarts on pods showing CUDA errors. also we should set max_restarts backoff to avoid thundering herd. we can patch the deployment with `spec.strategy.rollingUpdate.maxUnavailable=1`.

aisha (ml-infra): running nvidia-smi dmon and collecting per-process memory: looks like during hang some processes hit OOM on GPU and kernel driver triggered reset. attaching sample:
```
# nvidia-smi pmon -s um
# PID  GPU  MEM
12345  0    12345MB
23456  1    16384MB <-- at limit
```

maria (support): customer update sent: "We're investigating GPU infrastructure instability affecting multi-GPU models; can isolate to a small set of nodes. Mitigation in progress. Will update in 30m."

sre-oncall: doing the cordon/drain on gpu-n3-17 now (will move ongoing jobs to fallback pool). running kubectl drain; will watch `kubectl get pods -n redwood-serving` for crash loops and then restart single pods.

raj (runtime): deployed canary fallback route for tp4-family to `tp4-single` model in region-us-east-1 (trafficRouting: 10% -> single, 90% -> tp4). Will increase to 30% if errors persist.

incident-bot: ACTIONS TAKEN: nodes cordoned: gpu-n3-17,gpu-n3-18. 4 pods restarted with NCCL env overrides. Canary route applied.

kevin (eng-runtime): still seeing one pod spit `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION` after env changes. suspect driver binary mismatch on that host. scheduling remote SSH to collect /var/log/nvidia and kernel modules. assigning to @kevin (eng-runtime).

aisha (ml-infra): beginning rollback test on one node to previous driver v525.85. start ETA ~10m; will monitor for Xid resets.

sre-oncall: customer impact so far: customers saw transient increased failures ~14:00-14:22 UTC; after canary and targeted restarts error rate dropped to baseline for most routes. still seeing occasional NCCL TIMEOUTs on long pipeline steps.

maria (support): updating customers: "We've applied targeted restarts and routing fallbacks; some jobs were retried automatically. We're monitoring and will follow up with root cause once postmortem complete."

raj (runtime): for post-incident debug, please capture a full `LD_PRELOAD` backtrace + `gdb` on a failing container if we get another reproducible crash. also collect /tmp/nccl-debug-*.log from pods.

kevin (eng-runtime): driver rollback on gpu-n3-18 completed; no new GPU resets in last 6 minutes. rolling gpu-n3-17 now.

aisha (ml-infra): confirmed: after rollback node-level GPU resets stopped and NCCL hang rate dropped to near zero on rolled nodes.

sre-oncall: current status: partial mitigation successful. nodes rolled back or cordoned. Canary at 10% -> increasing to 25% in 5m. continuing monitoring. Postmortem owners: kevin (eng-runtime) + raj (runtime) + aisha (ml-infra).

maria (support): CS notified customers with follow-up ETA for RCA in 48 hours.

incident-bot: next update scheduled in 30 minutes. oncall handoff planned after stabilization window (2 hours) to daytime shift.

sre-oncall: handoff: I'll stay until 16:15 UTC or until nodes stable for 30m. if anyone sees fresh Xid 79 / GPU panic logs, ping with `urgent` and include node name.

kevin (eng-runtime): immediate action items:
- finish rollbacks for gpu-n3 pool (in progress)
- collect nv-hosttrace + driver rpm list on affected nodes
- open infra change to prevent auto-driver rollouts until regression tested with TP/PP workloads

raj (runtime): postmortem checklist:
- collect nccl logs and trace for 1 failing run
- reproduce in staging with same driver/kernel combo
- evaluate adding runtime guard: fallback to non-collective path if communicator shows early timeouts

aisha (ml-infra): will prepare canary test harness that runs short TP/PP workloads to smoke-test driver/kernel combos pre-rollout.

maria (support): closing in-thread support loop; will reopen if customers report reoccurrence.

incident-bot: declaring incident status: MITIGATION IN PROGRESS -> PARTIAL MITIGATION (nodes rolled back, traffic partially routed). Follow-up: RCA + postmortem required.

sre-oncall: thanks team. I'll paste final status and link to postmortem doc in ~45m. handing off to daytime after stabilization.
